svg.title: Past search schematic 09: Cave 3 (3Q): where the Copper Scroll was found, and the digs of 1952 and 1986
svg.text: Past searches 09 — Cave 3 (3Q): where the Copper Scroll was found, and the digs of 1952 and 1986
Schematic plan and section from the published descriptions. Blue = dug (who, when). Ink = the copper rolls. Grey = not recorded.
1952: H. de Contenson's team, dated 14–25 March in DJD III; rolls found 20 March. 1986: re-excavation reported by J. Patrich (ESI 6).
3Q = site 8 of 1952 (DJD III p. 6), plotted at Palestine grid 193.486 / 129.756 (±30 m; sheet 01), about 2 km N of Kh. Qumran (RB 60 p. 555).
Plan (widths to scale; outlines schematic; not oriented)
c. 10 m from W to E, under
cavity almost full of rat nests
two copper rolls, one on the
No north arrow: the repo gives no bearing for
the cave's axis, so the rolls' corner (the
chamber's north corner, near its entrance) is
Not to scale, except the 30–40 cm figures (vertical bar).
Below the grey dashed line nothing is recorded.
just in front of the rolls
About ten days under H. de Contenson, “fouillée dans toute son étendue”
(RB 60 p. 555). Clearing of the front, and depth reached: not stated.
April 1986, reported by J. Patrich (ESI 6 pp. 68–70; plan and sections,
Fig. 29). The extent and depth of the dig are not in the repo.
2.40 m: three sheets riveted end to end
The large roll holds two sheets still joined; the small roll is the
dug; extent or depth not stated
Where the jars lay. RB 60 p. 555: sherds very numerous in the inner
chamber, few under the entrance blocks. DJD III pp. 7–8: the mass of
jars lay in front of the chamber; inside it, very few sherds.
How many jars. RB 60: about 40 jars, 26 lids. DJD III: 35 jars (5

spared them, so after they were laid (inference). ESI 6: the roof fell
0.30–0.40 m. DJD III: the jar layer's thickness. ESI 6: the documents'
depth. Whether it is one measurement is not stated.
Size. Reed 1954 p. 12 (ledger S01): about 10 m wide, 3 m deep, 2 m
high before the roof fell. RB 60 p. 555: the front's height is not
1952: DJD III and RB 60. 1986: ESI 6, as summarised in the repo.

Rat-nest cavity: textile, leather, one inscribed fragment.

near its entrance (RB 60), a little apart from the jars.
No skin or papyrus fragment was collected near them (DJD

The documents had lain 0.30–0.40 m deep, in shallow
recesses. The excavator dates their placing to the Second
Temple period, after the roof fell.
No further copper document or deposit reported (S11).

To scale, at 0.5 m per cubit (sheet 04). The scroll names no
deposit in 3Q: this only compares sizes.
DJD III, Textes (1962) pp. 6–8, 14–15, 201 (de Vaux); RB 60 (1953) pp. 555–558 (de Vaux); ESI 6
(1987/88) pp. 68–70, Fig. 29 (Patrich), via the repo's review; ledger rows S01 and S11 (Reed 1954 p.
12 via S01); point 8 of the 1952 map; sheet 04 for the scroll's depths.
Schematic, after the texts of DJD III and RB 60; layout only roughly after ESI 6 Fig. 29, not traced.
To scale: the 10 m width and 3 × 2 m chamber in plan, the 30–40 cm figures in section, the copper
band, the depth strip. All else schematic; the plan is not oriented.
Where 1952 found the rolls, the jars and the fragments, and what 1986 adds. Both campaigns are
recorded as digs, but neither gives the depth it reached. The documents lay 0.30–0.40 m deep.
The cave's bearing or original entrance, or how deep either campaign dug. Anything about the scroll's
own deposits: 3Q is where the scroll was found, not a place it names.
